market_mood: Two shocks dominate: Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as Nvidia CEO over a security scandal, and a fresh escalation in the Gulf with tankers struck in the Strait of Hormuz lifting oil while gold slid to a one-year low. Deal news is busy too, with a $3.2B bank merger, a failed Global Payments buyout, and bolt-on acquisitions across industrials and tech.
self_check: My oil and energy calls have been badly wrong lately (1 of 11 over the last two weeks) and high-confidence calls have been my worst bucket, so today I leaned on merger and geopolitics ideas, kept confidence at medium or low, and avoided direct crude plays.

picks.reason: Hancock Whitney agreed to buy Trustmark in a ~$3.2B all-stock deal; target shares in bank mergers often keep grinding toward the exchange ratio over following weeks.
IBM bought identity-security firm AuthMind, adding to its software/cyber mix; it is also a relative safe haven in tech while Nvidia leadership risk weighs on semis.
Acquirer in a scale-building Gulf South bank merger.
Takeover chatter in household products could re-rate the whole group.
Missile-defense exposure as Gulf attacks continue.

watchlist_notes.note: Flat-to-firm after a strong week, but an Nvidia leadership shock plus Hormuz tensions are two fresh sources of volatility.
Most exposed index to the Nvidia CEO resignation, since semis carry heavy weight in the Nasdaq 100.

Less tech-heavy, so it may hold up better than the Nasdaq if the Nvidia story keeps pressuring chips.
Record run and heavy options activity as investors treat it as a safe harbor in tech, though UBS notes growth now leans on price hikes.
No major company news; indirectly in focus via Alphabet TPU and AI capex chatter.
Routine news on skills training and warehouse robotics; AWS alumni moving to Meta infrastructure is a mild talent signal.

Debate over its $27B off-balance-sheet AI data center financing keeps a cloud over the stock after a 12% monthly drop.
No major news; rival commentary on robotaxis versus car ownership is the only relevant item.
No major news; Dimon's debt-burden comments and regional bank M&A are the backdrop.
Oil up over $1 on Hormuz tanker explosions, and energy stocks were rising pre-bell.

Inflation fears from higher oil are a headwind for long-dated Treasuries.

top_buys.pitch: All-stock takeover target that should converge toward deal value.
top_buys.why: Hancock Whitney agreed to buy Trustmark for roughly $3.2 billion in stock. Targets in all-stock regional bank deals usually trade at a discount to the exchange ratio at first and close the gap over weeks as the deal is seen as likely to complete. My merger-themed calls have been my best category this year.
top_buys.risks: If Hancock Whitney's shares fall, the implied value of the deal falls with them, and regulators or shareholders could object.
top_buys.watch: Proxy filings, regulatory approvals, and Hancock Whitney's own share price.

top_buys.pitch: Cyber bolt-on plus a safe-haven bid while chip leadership is in doubt.
top_buys.why: IBM acquired identity-security company AuthMind, extending its higher-margin software and security franchise. With Nvidia's CEO gone and semis wobbling, money often rotates toward steadier enterprise tech with recurring revenue. IBM's AI consulting backlog gives it exposure to the theme without the chip-cycle risk.
top_buys.risks: IBM is a slow grower and can lag badly if the broad tech rally resumes and investors chase high-beta names instead.
top_buys.watch: Software segment growth and any further security acquisitions.

top_buys.pitch: Acquirer in a scale-building Gulf South bank merger.
top_buys.why: Hancock Whitney is buying Trustmark in a $3.2 billion all-stock deal that adds meaningful deposit scale in overlapping markets. Acquirer shares usually dip on announcement and recover as cost-synergy math gets appreciated. Regional bank consolidation has been a profitable theme this year.
top_buys.risks: Acquirers often lag for months, and dilution or integration costs could weigh.
top_buys.watch: Synergy targets disclosed in the investor presentation.

top_buys.pitch: Takeover chatter in household products could re-rate the whole group.
top_buys.why: Clorox jumped on speculation of takeover interest, which tends to make investors look again at cheap, defensive consumer staples peers. Staples are the worst-performing sector of the past week at +0.2%, leaving room for a catch-up bid. Colgate is a low-volatility name, which suits a modest idea.
top_buys.risks: Takeover chatter fades fast, and staples can keep lagging in a risk-on tape.
top_buys.watch: Whether any formal bid for Clorox materializes.

top_buys.pitch: Missile-defense exposure as Gulf attacks continue.
top_buys.why: Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia and tanker explosions in Hormuz point to continued demand for interceptors and air-defense systems. Northrop is a core supplier in that chain. Defense budgets respond to sustained conflict rather than single headlines, so the move can unfold slowly.
top_buys.risks: Any Iran de-escalation or spending cuts would deflate the trade quickly.
top_buys.watch: New defense contract awards and the Gulf security situation.

summary.big_story: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned over a security scandal while tanker explosions in the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil higher and gold to a one-year low.
summary.top_pick: Trustmark, newly agreed to be bought by Hancock Whitney in a $3.2B all-stock deal, as bank-merger targets tend to keep drifting toward deal value.
summary.watch: Watch how semiconductors trade without Huang at the helm and whether further Hormuz incidents keep a risk premium in crude.
